vsm2.12:2.1: 1. Āneñja—“imperturbability”: a term normally used for the four immaterial states, together with the fourth jhāna. See also §16f., and MN 106.
vsm2.12:10.2: 2. Giribhaṇḍavahanapūjā: Vism-mhṭ (p. 375) says: “Giribhaṇḍa-vahanapūjā nāma Cetiyagiriṃ ādiṃ katvā sakaladīpe samudde ca yāva yojanā mahatī dīpapūjā (‘it is a name for a great island-offering starting with the Cetiyagiri (Mihintale) and extending over the whole island and up to a league into the sea ’).” Mentioned in A-a to AN 1:1; M-a II 398; and Mahāvaṃsa XXXIV.81.
vsm2.12:12.4: 3. These are the four headings of the roads to power (see §50).
vsm2.12:19.4: 4. I.e. one wants it to be known that he can practice jhāna.
vsm2.12:20.4: 5. “It counter-strikes (paṭiharati), thus it is a counter-stroke (pāṭihāriya—metamorphosis = miracle). What strikes out (harati), removes, what is counter to it (paṭipakkha) is therefore called counter-striking (paṭihāriya), since what is counter-striking strikes out anything counter (paṭipakkha) to itself. Paṭihāriya (counter-striking) is the same as pāṭihāriya (counter-stroke = metamorphosis = miracle)” (Vism-mhṭ 379).
